2607.26977.title: TREK: A Travel Reasoning and Evaluation Kit for LLM Agents in Complex Trip Planning
2607.26977.paper_summary: Travel planning is a demanding stress test for tool-using LLM agents: a usable itinerary is a single artifact that must be right along many axes at once - every flight, hotel, and attraction must exist and be bookable, the days must be physically traversable, the total must clear a budget, and the plan must serve a traveler whose needs are only partly stated. Existing agent benchmarks reward these properties one at a time and grade the final output with soft or LLM-judged rubrics, which cannot certify that a returned plan is executable and are neither reproducible nor auditable. We introduce TREK (Travel Reasoning and Evaluation Kit), a benchmark for feasible itinerary synthesis: producing a single plan that is jointly constraint-correct, hallucination-free, spatio-temporally executable, budget-valid, and responsive to the traveler's unstated persona needs. TREK comprises 800 multi-constraint tasks - 533 feasible and 267 provably infeasible with typed route/entity/budget causes - over a synthetic, internally consistent knowledge base of 212,530 records across 375 cities and 13 personas, served through a production-style tool sandbox of validated RESTful APIs. Every task is scored by a fully deterministic, rule-based evaluator with no LLM judge and ships a human-verified gold reference that scores a perfect 1.0 under that same evaluator, so the ceiling is demonstrably achievable and every remaining gap is an agent limitation rather than scorer strictness. Evaluating 15 LLM agents across nine constraint dimensions, we find that even the strongest (GPT-5.6) produces a fully-feasible plan on only 46.2% of solvable tasks, with a median of 6.6% and a floor of 0.0%; satisfying travelers' unstated needs emerges as the universal bottleneck, unsolved even at the frontier. We release the dataset, tool sandbox, deterministic evaluator, and agent code as a fully reproducible benchmark.
2607.26977.paper_summary_zh: 旅行規劃對於使用工具的 LLM 代理來說是一個要求苛刻的壓力測試：可用的行程是一個單一的產物，必須在多個方面同時正確——每一個航班、酒店和景點都必須存在並且可預訂，行程中的天數必須可以實際走訪，總費用必須符合預算，計劃必須滿足旅行者的需求，而這些需求僅部分被陳述。現有的代理基準一次只獎勵這些屬性，並用柔性或 LLM 評判的標準來評分最終輸出，這無法證明所返回的計劃是可執行的，且既不可重現也不可審計。我們推出了 TREK（旅行推理與評估工具包），這是一個可行行程合成的基準：生成一個共同約束正確、無幻覺、時空可執行、預算有效且能響應旅行者未陳述的個性需求的單一計劃。TREK 包含 800 個多約束任務——533 個可行和 267 個可證明不可行的任務，並附有類型化的路徑/實體/預算原因——基於一個合成的、內部一致的知識庫，該知識庫包含 212,530 條記錄，涵蓋 375 個城市和 13 種人設，通過一個生產風格的工具沙盒，提供經過驗證的 RESTful API。每個任務由一個完全確定性的、基於規則的評估器進行評分，沒有 LLM 評判，並提供一個經人類驗證的金標準，該標準在同一評估器下得分為完美的 1.0，因此上限是明確可達的，所有剩餘的差距都是代理的限制，而非評分的嚴格性。在九個約束維度上評估 15 個 LLM 代理，我們發現即使是最強的（GPT-5.6）在可解任務中僅能生成 46.2% 的完全可行計劃，中位數為 6.6%，最低為 0.0%；滿足旅行者的未陳述需求成為普遍的瓶頸，即使在最前沿也未得到解決。我們釋放數據集、工具沙盒、確定性評估器和代理代碼，作為一個完全可重現的基準。
